Draw the estimand from its sampling distribution

Source: R/draws.R
pollin_draws.Rd

Returns draws of the two G-computation arm means of a fitted estimand (the predictions under the high and the low arm, averaged over the rows of the model data, as in pollin_effects()) and the estimand formed from each pair of draws on the estimand's scale and basis. A quantity computed from the estimand is then computed per draw and summarised last.

Usage

pollin_draws(
  x,
  n = 4000L,
  method = c("simulation", "bootstrap", "posterior"),
  response = NULL,
  seed = NULL
)

Arguments

x

A pollin_fit() object.

n

Number of draws.

method

"simulation" (the default for a glmmTMB fit), "bootstrap", or "posterior" (for a flexyBayes fit).

response

The response to draw. Required when the fit holds more than one response.

seed

Optional seed for the draws. The session's random number state is restored afterwards. Posterior draws with a seed set both R's generator and INLA's, and are reproducible.

Value

An object of class pollin_draws: a list holding

  • high, low: numeric matrices of draws of the arm means, one row per draw and one column per level of the fit's by column, or a single column "overall" when the fit has no by;

  • estimate: the matrix of the estimand on its scale and basis, formed from high and low draw by draw;

  • estimand, response, by, method, engine, n (the number of draws), seed, and population (the pollin_population() object, or NULL for the trial population).

Details

Three methods are available:

  • "simulation" (the default for a glmmTMB fit) draws the fixed effects from their estimated sampling distribution, a multivariate normal centred on the estimates with their covariance matrix, and recomputes the arm means for each draw. Every row keeps its estimated random effects, the prediction rule of pollin_effects(), so the draws carry the uncertainty in the fixed effects only, like the delta interval.

  • "bootstrap" keeps the arm means of the parametric bootstrap refits that pollin_effects() runs with interval = "bootstrap": responses are simulated from the fitted model (new random effects included) and the model is refitted to each simulated set. With the same seed and n = n_boot, the percentile interval of the draws is the bootstrap interval of pollin_effects(). Refits that fail are dropped, with a warning, so the number of draws can be smaller than n.

  • "posterior", the default and the only method for a fit with engine = "flexyBayes", draws the fixed effects, the random effects and the variance parameters jointly from the posterior (flexyBayes::fb_inla_posterior_sample()) and recomputes the arm means for each draw with the prediction rule of pollin_effects(): every row keeps its own random effects, here the drawn ones, and under each arm a row takes its unit's effect for that arm.

When the estimand refers to a population declared with pollin_population(), a further column "population" holds the population arm means, the area-weighted sums of the stratum arm means, and the estimand formed from them: a ratio of population means, not a weighted mean of the stratum estimands.

See also

pollin_effects() for estimates and intervals; pollin_population() for a population of strata.

Examples

# \donttest{
set.seed(1)
d <- data.frame(
  trt = rep(rep(c("Cage", "Open"), each = 10L), 8L),
  Site = rep(paste0("s", seq_len(8L)), each = 20L)
)
d$pods <- rnbinom(nrow(d), mu = exp(3 + 0.3 * (d$trt == "Open")), size = 10)
pd <- pollin_data(d, "pods", "trt", unit = "Site")
ds <- pollin_design(pd, c(excluded = "Cage", open = "Open"), "rcbd")
est <- pollin_estimand(ds, "dependence", "ratio", "loss")
dr <- pollin_draws(pollin_fit(est), n = 2000L, seed = 1L)
dr
#> <pollin_draws>
#>   family   : dependence (E2) 
#>   scale    : ratio 
#>   basis    : loss 
#>   estimate : 1 - Cage/Open (loss share) 
#>   response : pods 
#>   method   : simulation of the fixed effects 
#>   engine   : glmmTMB 
#>   draws    : 2000 
#>   columns  : overall 
#>   note     : simulation draws cover fixed-effect uncertainty only
summary(dr)
#>   response   level    median  conf.low conf.high     family scale basis
#> 1     pods overall 0.2691091 0.1741931 0.3524436 dependence ratio  loss
#>       method    n
#> 1 simulation 2000
# }
